I'll begin this post by saying that, in an ironic twist of fate, my wife is currently away to her home state to visit her grandparents for what might be the final time, after news of their failing health had reached us.

I had to remain home due to work, but I took the opportunity to invite my mother and sister over for a home-cooked meal and a few drinks. It had been too long since the 3 of us had sat down and caught up, ever since us kids flew the coop, but that seems to be the way of my family. Actually, shortly after we left my parents separated but I'll stick to the topic in the title of this post -- I've begun to think that I could use my family as inspiration to fill a number of books on a variety of subjects without even touching on my brother.

While enjoying a glass of wine that reminds me of my birthplace, the conversation turned to the inevitable subject of Health and Wellness. I mentioned to them that my father, who is an avid selfy taker (I know, right?), seemed to look more and more ill as the seasons passed this year. My sister agreed but said that, unfortunately, my father will not speak about his health with her anymore.

He'd had a cancer scare a few years back, which he did not mention to us until the very day of the procedure but which did explain his destructive behaviour, during which he has told us all that the doctor was successful in isolating and cutting off blood-flow to the tumor.

I'd had a similar experience with him over the last couple of years: Each time I would ask a question pertaining to his health and his cancer, he would act as if he didn't hear me and simply wait for me to ask a different one.

How am I to look at him over the Christmas Dinner table, laden with roast pork and lamb, fresh bread, and sweet cakes, and speak with him as if all is perfectly fine when his health and the future of our family might be changing in one of the most dramatic ways possible?

Should I press the issue if my questions fall on deaf ears again?
